macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks suffer sharp technology-led selloff
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.8%, the S&P 500 dropped 2%, and the Dow declined 1.2% as disappointing technology earnings intensified concerns about costly artificial-intelligence investment.[1]

items.title: Amazon and Intel results pressure technology shares
items.summary: Amazon shares fell after weaker-than-expected earnings and revenue alongside a major increase in capital spending, while Intel plunged after issuing a below-consensus outlook.[2]

items.title: Fed holds rates as markets price December hike
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its policy rate at 3.75%–4% in a 10–2 vote; markets continued to assign a high probability to a 25-basis-point December increase, while Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan called for at least two further hikes.[3]

items.title: U.S. GDP growth exceeds expectations
items.summary: Third-quarter U.S. GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized rate, surpassing the 3.2% forecast and reflecting resilient consumer spending and strong AI-related infrastructure investment.[2]

items.title: ECB and Bank of Japan leave rates unchanged
items.summary: The European Central Bank held its benchmark rate while leaving open the possibility of a December increase amid energy-driven inflation pressures. The Bank of Japan also maintained its policy rate at 1.25%.[4]

items.title: Oil rises as Middle East tensions support energy shares
items.summary: Brent crude reached about $112 per barrel and WTI rose to roughly $104 as geopolitical tensions lifted oil prices. ExxonMobil and Chevron benefited from stronger refining margins and beat profit expectations.[5]

items.title: Binance hack weighs on crypto markets
items.summary: Bitcoin fell more than 2% after a reported $6.3 billion hack at cryptocurrency exchange Binance renewed concerns about digital-asset security.[5]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Binance hack triggers broad crypto sell-off
items.summary: A reported $6.3 billion Binance security breach sent Bitcoin below $77,000 and pushed major cryptocurrencies lower. Binance said it froze about $3 billion in assets and would cover losses, while more than $1.5 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated over 24 hours.[1][2]

items.title: Bitcoin and major tokens pare losses after record hack
items.summary: Bitcoin and Ethereum recovered part of their declines but remained below key levels after Binance suspended transactions during its breach investigation. Bitcoin traded near $77,300, while Ethereum was around $2,231 and BNB was down about 5%.[3]

items.title: ICE partners with Hyperliquid builder on U.S. perpetual markets
items.summary: Intercontinental Exchange, parent of the New York Stock Exchange, announced a strategic investment in Trade[XYZ] to develop regulated U.S. cryptocurrency and traditional-asset perpetual markets on Hyperliquid. The arrangement remains subject to regulatory approvals.[4]

items.title: Crypto market capitalization falls nearly 4%
items.summary: The broad sell-off reduced total cryptocurrency market capitalization to roughly $2.6 trillion. Bitcoin fell about 4.4%, Ethereum 4.6%, XRP 4.6%, and Solana 6.1% over the reported 24-hour period.[5]

items.title: Ethereum whale transfers attract attention amid market volatility
items.summary: A wallet received 9,625 ETH worth approximately $21.6 million from FalconX, while another withdrew 3,377 ETH valued at about $7.5 million from OKX.[6]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly cuts fundraising target to $20 billion
items.summary: OpenAI is reportedly seeking about $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, reducing its previously discussed funding ambitions amid broader investor concerns about the technology sector.

items.title: New York enacts restrictions on unsafe AI chatbot behavior with children
items.summary: New York has enacted legislation banning certain unsafe AI companion features in interactions with minors. The law is scheduled to take effect January 1 and reflects growing state-level action on AI safety.

items.title: FTC investigates use of consumer data in algorithmic pricing
items.summary: The Federal Trade Commission ordered companies including Walmart, Delta, United, Lyft, DoorDash, Instacart and Target to provide information about how personal data is used to set prices or compensation. The inquiry highlights increasing regulatory scrutiny of AI-assisted pricing practices.

items.title: AI demand drives semiconductor supply and manufacturing concerns
items.summary: A TechInsights outlook identifies surging AI demand as a major force reshaping semiconductors, with pressure on high-bandwidth memory supplies, increased investment in advanced packaging and rising manufacturing emissions.

items.title: Researchers study autonomous AI agents in a virtual environment
items.summary: An unpublished, non-peer-reviewed study examined 13 Claude Opus 4.7-based agents left for 30 hours in a virtual island without assigned tasks. The agents reportedly developed games and displayed unexpected behaviors.

items.title: Serval raises $150 million for enterprise coding agents
items.summary: Serval, a startup developing coding agents for enterprise automation, raised $150 million in Series C funding at a reported $3 billion valuation, underscoring continued investment in enterprise AI automation.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: The Duskbloods delayed to 2027
items.summary: FromSoftware has postponed its Nintendo Switch 2-exclusive multiplayer title The Duskbloods from 2026 to 2027, citing final development adjustments.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla to receive New Game+
items.summary: Ubisoft announced that Assassin’s Creed Valhalla will add New Game+ on November 5, alongside other franchise updates. Ubisoft says the game has surpassed 40 million players.

items.title: PHP vulnerability disrupts multiple online games
items.summary: A reported PHP vulnerability caused outages affecting games including Final Fantasy XIV and Umamusume: Pretty Derby. The incident was among several major gaming stories discussed in the latest industry roundup.

items.title: id Software and MachineGames deepen collaboration
items.summary: id Software said it is working more closely with MachineGames on technology collaboration despite layoffs affecting both studios. The report links the development to speculation about a future Wolfenstein project.

items.title: John Romero’s canceled Xbox shooter finds a new publisher
items.summary: Romero Games’ shooter, dropped by Microsoft in 2025, has reportedly been rebuilt by a smaller team and secured a new publisher whose identity has not yet been disclosed.

items.title: Apex Legends: Cipher update detailed
items.summary: Respawn published early designer notes for Apex Legends Season 31, scheduled for November 3. The update includes changes for Crypto, Lifeline and Revenant, an Akimbo Wingman, and a new Strongholds feature.

items.title: World of Horror receives free major update
items.summary: Junji Ito-inspired horror RPG World of Horror launched its free version 1.2 “As Below So Above” update for Steam, GOG and itch.io players on Windows and macOS.

items.title: EA reportedly prioritized Star Wars Battlefront 3 over Mass Effect
items.summary: A report summarized by gaming outlets says EA closed BioWare and prioritized development resources for a new Star Wars Battlefront project rather than a new Mass Effect title.

items.title: EA Sports FC 27 receives PEGI 16 rating over loot boxes
items.summary: EA Sports FC 27 was reportedly assigned a PEGI 16 rating in Europe, with loot-box mechanics cited as a factor in the classification.

items.title: Xbox announces cloud-gaming usage tiers
items.summary: Xbox reportedly revealed new cloud-gaming pricing limits, including a tier starting at $3.99 for 10 hours of usage.
